title: Compliance-Gap Decomposition Across Open-Weight Model Families

original_idea.body:
# Compliance-Gap Decomposition Across Open-Weight Model Families

**Problem:** Alignment faking shows a compliance gap (e.g., 35% for Claude 3 Opus). A recent decomposition splits this into competing drivers, and gaps were replicated in OLMo, Gemma, Llama. But no study systematically decomposes the gap's DRIVERS across small open models you can actually run yourself.

**Direction:** Replicate the free-tier/paid-tier alignment-faking harness on 3-4 small/medium open models. Apply the three-driver decomposition (e.g., genuine objection vs instrumental compliance vs incoherence) by ablating prompt components and classifying CoT. Report which driver dominates per model and whether the gap survives in models small enough for a consumer GPU.

**Why it matters:** Tests whether alignment faking is a frontier-only phenomenon or a general property, and what mechanism produces it - central to building scheming safety cases. Uses published open harness, no training, single GPU.

**Relevant context:** arXiv 2412.14093 (Alignment Faking in LLMs) is the original. greaterwrong 'What Drives the Compliance Gap? A Three-Driver Decomposition'. AlignmentForum 'Alignment Faking Revisited: Improved Classifiers and Open Source Extensions' replicates gaps in OLMo-3.1-32B, Gemma-3-27B, Llama-3.3-70B.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: decomposing alignment-faking drivers across open families informs scheming safety cases, a critical pathway.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Replicate a published harness + ablation + CoT classification; guided, though decomposition logic is intermediate.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused per-model dominant-driver report; ablation + classification is multi-step but bounded.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Open harness, no training; tests whether faking is frontier-only, externally valuable.

low_compute.reasoning: Replicated gaps used 27-70B models; small/medium open models push consumer-GPU limits, single mid-GPU days at best.

novelty.reasoning: Decomposition method exists and gaps replicated; cross-small-family driver decomposition is partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Decomposition exists; small-family driver analysis partly open.
